proposed_statement_changes.reason: The original statement combines a provable result for the explicit saturated one-step map with unproved assertions about the heavy-light point estimate, variance, and radius, which are only prose handles. The active directive expressly requires retention of only the one-step conclusions when no explicit globally honest Gaussian/fallback hybrid score has been installed. This narrowing keeps the identical balanced triangular class; it does not substitute a smaller model, and it removes only conclusions involving the undefined heavy-light outputs.

proposed.justification: This theorem establishes the regular balanced-submodel limit law for the explicit saturated-cell one-step estimator without attributing any property to an undefined heavy-light output.
proposed.gap: The result verifies directly that cellwise nuisance errors have weighted rate \(d_n/n\), so orthogonality gives an \(o_P(n^{-1/2})\) remainder when \(d_n=o(\sqrt n)\). It does not establish endpoint equivalence for the proposed globally honest interval.
proposed.consumer: It supplies the valid Gaussian benchmark for the \(n=9915,d=8196\) saturated 401(k) analysis when the declared balanced triangular conditions are scientifically defensible.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Synchronize the dependencies, free symbols, and statement notes with the proposed one-step-only claim; the proof no longer consumes either heavy-light construction handle or the unresolved rare-tail node.

proposed.comparator_claim: Theorem 2 on pages 8--10 lower-bounds worst-case mean squared error for the one-arm functional \(\psi_1\) by the order of \(n^{-1}+d^2/[n^2\log^2 n]\) under fixed overlap; Appendix C.5 sets the control-arm regression to zero in the hard family.
The paper constructs heavy-light best-polynomial factorial-moment estimators attaining minimax mean squared error for additive discrete-distribution functionals.

Sections 4.1--4.2 provide scalar bounded-influence score inequalities, but they do not prove a tail theorem for this pilot-selected marked-factorial statistic; moreover, the symmetric half-log transform stipulated in the current directive is not globally monotone and therefore needs an additional retained-range or score replacement before root inversion is valid.
Theorem 1 lower-bounds expected confidence length in Gaussian nonparametric experiments by a between-class modulus and the paper constructs constant-factor adaptive intervals.
Theorem 5.1 gives uniformly valid asymptotically efficient Gaussian ATE intervals from cross-fitted orthogonal scores under nuisance-rate conditions.

The Abstract and Sections 2--4 derive finite-sample optimal bias-aware ATE estimators and confidence intervals under smoothness or shape restrictions when regression errors are normal with known variance, with feasible asymptotic extensions for unknown errors.

Theorem 3.1 gives a self-normalized moderate-deviation expansion for fixed-order nondegenerate Studentized U-statistics under moment conditions; its degree-one consequence is used only for the oracle-score central limit step.
The paper gives nearly tight dimension-free confidence intervals for probabilities of individually unobserved multinomial events.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The local claim now matches only the explicit saturated one-step DML benchmark, and the Catoni positioning must record the proved nonmonotonicity obstruction rather than promise a completed selected-factorial calibration.

open_obligations.what_is_open: An explicit data-measurable rare-cell score interval with a directly proved tail event, sharp expected radius, and certified root inversion for the pilot-selected marked-factorial statistic.
open_obligations.obstruction: The stipulated transform \(\psi(x)=\tfrac12\log\{(1+x+x^2/2)/(1-x+x^2/2)\}\) satisfies \(\psi'(x)=2(2-x^2)/(x^4+4)\), so it is not globally monotone. For odd \(B\ge3\), block values consisting of \(B-1\) zeros and one sufficiently remote value make the summed score change sign at least three times; thus the requested unique root, monotone score inversion, and a uniform positive slope modulus do not follow. In addition, conditioning on the common pilot controls fluctuations about a pilot-dependent block mean, not automatically about the unconditional expectation appearing in the target. The frozen bank supplies a factorial covariance calculation but neither a pilot-fluctuation score nor a retained range that repairs these two gaps.
open_obligations.attempted: I instantiated the directed constants \(K=\lfloor\alpha_0\log(em)\rfloor\), pilot threshold \(256\log(em)\), and mass scale \(4096\log(em)/m\), and set up the ordered-index overlap enumeration for a conditional block variance calculation. Before using an MGF inequality, I differentiated the exact proposed score and tested its root equation. That audit fails at uniqueness and monotone inversion, independently of any forbidden MSE-to-Chebyshev conversion, so asserting the requested block-tail certificate would skip an earlier necessary step.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Finite-sample coverage and expected-radius bounds for an explicit heavy-light interval on the unrestricted global class.
open_obligations.obstruction: The rare score is unresolved for the reasons recorded on \(oeq:observable\text{-}rare\text{-}tail\). The heavy branch is also not a sample map: no winsorization threshold, deterministic fourth-moment truncation allowance, aggregate self-normalized score, Gaussian/fallback switching rule, or score radius is defined. Consequently neither allocated score event can be proved, and the all-heavy identity required for local equivalence is absent. The deterministic light-bias lemma cannot imply honesty.
open_obligations.attempted: I decomposed the ATE error into pilot, light bias, light fluctuation, heavy truncation bias, and heavy fluctuation terms and allocated the requested \(\alpha/4,\alpha/4,\alpha/2\) error levels. Only the deterministic light-bias term closes from the current core. The proposed symmetric score fails the root audit before a direct MGF proof, and there is no heavy summand on which to perform the corresponding fourth-moment calculation.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A certified outward root enclosure and the claimed bit complexity for the actual statistical score equations.
open_obligations.obstruction: The coefficient and factorial magnitude envelope can be propagated by interval arithmetic, but endpoint error requires converting score error into root error. The stipulated score is nonmonotone and has zero derivative at \(\pm\sqrt2\); no retained bracket with a positive slope modulus is defined. Thus bisection is not certified and the frozen working-precision formula cannot yield the claimed uniform endpoint tolerance. The exact-real heavy score is also absent.
open_obligations.attempted: I propagated the banked coefficient bound \(6^{2K}\) through the declared \((en)^{8L_n}\) magnitude envelope and verified the deterministic inclusion, coverage-monotonicity, and length consequences of outward endpoint enclosures. The missing slope bound prevents completing the root and bit-count induction.

prose_updates.tldr: The identified ATE and the banked four-coordinate light-cell approximation are valid, and this round proves the regular balanced-submodel expansion, variance consistency, and Gaussian limit for the explicit cross-fitted saturated one-step estimator. The proposed globally honest heavy-light interval is not yet a theorem: its rare-cell score uses a symmetric half-log transform that is not globally monotone, while its heavy branch and Gaussian/fallback hybrid are not explicit sample maps. Therefore the uniform upper frontier, certified numerical interval, and heavy-light endpoint equivalence remain open rather than being inferred from the banked mean-squared-error calculation.

project_justification.gap: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024 supplies the large-alphabet point-risk obstruction and documents uncertain Gaussian/bootstrap coverage in the \(n=9915,d=8196\) 401(k) application, but not an honest expected-length theorem. The accepted heterogeneity run supplies the one-mark factorial approximation and bias architecture, not a direct confidence-tail calibration. Catoni2012 supplies scalar score inequalities; it does not validate the nonmonotone symmetric half-log root prescribed here or control the common-pilot fluctuation of a selected factorial statistic.
project_justification.niche: The unresolved contribution is an explicit globally honest interval for arbitrary categorical cell masses under fixed overlap and an absolute conditional fourth-moment envelope, together with a same-class confidence-length converse and a certified implementation. Any valid construction must calibrate the selected light statistic and the heavy branch directly, while switching to the efficient Gaussian radius on the balanced local regime.
project_justification.fill: The present core proves the imported light approximation bias and now proves the saturated one-step Gaussian benchmark under \(d_n=o(\sqrt n)\). It also isolates a concrete obstruction to the proposed calibration: the stipulated half-log score is redescending, can have several roots, and has no uniform slope for bisection. Completing the project requires replacing that score or proving a retained-range theorem, controlling pilot-dependent centering, and defining the heavy winsorized self-normalized Gaussian/fallback branch before the global, numerical, and endpoint claims can be restored.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The cross-fitted saturated-cell propensities and outcome regressions are explicit and have weighted squared-error order \(d_n/n\) on the balanced local class. The global pilot-selected light factorial statistic is explicit only through the banked compatibility handle; the proposed heavy robust score remains to be defined.
sampling_model.computation: Categorical and treatment coordinates are exact and real outcomes have dyadic enclosures. Coefficient and falling-factorial recurrences admit outward interval evaluation, but certified monotone bisection is not currently available because the stipulated symmetric half-log score is nonmonotone and can have zero derivative; a retained monotone bracket or a corrected score is required.

prose_updates.related_work: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024 remains the application and point-risk anchor: it treats arbitrary categorical masses, gives the one-arm large-alphabet lower rate, and reports the \(n=9915,d=8196\) 401(k) saturated analysis, but does not prove the present honest-length frontier. CausalSmithHeterogeneityFrontier2026 supplies the clipped real-mark Chebyshev factorial estimator and its bias/second-moment architecture; no tail theorem is imported from it. Catoni2012 provides scalar bounded-influence score inequalities, but the symmetric half-log formula stipulated in this run is redescending rather than globally monotone, so the source does not justify unique-root inversion here. ChernozhukovEtAl2018DML and Hahn1998 supply the regular efficient ATE benchmark; the narrowed local theorem verifies the required saturated-cell nuisance rates directly on the project-imposed balanced class. ShaoZhou2016 is used only for the degree-one oracle-score normal limit and does not cover the growing-degree selected factorial statistic. ArmstrongKolesar2021, CaiLow2004, and Painsky2022 remain adjacent comparators rather than sources of the missing global construction.
prose_updates.interpretation: On a balanced table with \(d_n=o(\sqrt n)\), the ordinary cross-fitted saturated one-step estimator has the familiar efficient Gaussian limit and a ratio-consistent score variance. This does not yet license reporting the proposed heavy-light interval: global honesty at the rare-cell transition still depends on a valid directly calibrated score and an explicit heavy branch.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: For the stipulated symmetric score, direct differentiation gives \(\psi'(x)=2(2-x^2)/(x^4+4)\). It is increasing only for \(|x|<\sqrt2\), decreases outside that range, tends back to zero in both tails, and can produce at least three roots for an odd collection of block values. Consequently uniqueness, monotone bisection, and a uniform score-to-root error modulus are false without an additional retained-range theorem. The common pilot creates a second issue: conditional block calibration is centered at a pilot-dependent mean, whereas the open target is centered at the unconditional expectation.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The global model continues to allow arbitrary and zero cell masses, fixed overlap, bounded cell means, and only an absolute conditional fourth-central-moment envelope; no standardized-kurtosis or positive cell-variance condition is added. Under those same assumptions, only the light approximation bias and the balanced-submodel saturated one-step limit are currently established. No finite-sample heavy-light coverage, sharp expected length, certified endpoint computation, or heavy-light Gaussian endpoint equivalence is claimed until the rare and heavy score constructions are made explicit and proved. The balanced mass and nondegenerate efficient-variance conditions remain local restrictions only.
